thread.title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) confronts lawsuits over older iPhone’s performance with latest software update

author: Grant Pasek
title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) confronts lawsuits over older iPhone’s performance with latest software update
text:
January 31, 2018 Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) confronts lawsuits over older iPhone’s performance with latest software update 
The troubles for Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) might be ongoing over its performance throttling on older iPhones. 
On Tuesday, Bloomberg reported that two federal agencies, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the US Department of Justice (DOJ), are investigating whether the company has violated any securities laws regarding disclosures that it reduced older iPhones performance having flagging batteries. 
According to Bloomberg report, referring to people having knowledge of the matter, the government has asked the company to provide information regarding the issue. The chairman of a U.S. Senate committee supervising business issues asked the company to answer questions concerning its disclosures, according to a Reuters report provided this month. 
The company has confessed in December that iPhone software could slow down some phones having battery problems. It said, aging lithium batteries supply power erratically, which might cause iPhones to shut down suddenly to protect the sensitive circuits inside. 
The company has posted a public apology while responding to disclosure of the throttling issue. The company has also announced that it will provide out-of-warranty iPhone battery replacements for $29 this year, much lower than the normal price of $79. 
Apple is projected to allow users turn off the feature that slows performance in order to preserve battery life, as part of the forthcoming iOS 11.3 update. 
So far, consumers have filed about 50 proposed class action lawsuits concerning Apple’s latest iPhone software update, which they claimed caused sudden shutdowns and weakened the performance of the SE, 6 and 7 lines iPhone models. They claim the company fooled consumers into believing their phones were approaching the end of their life cycle, compelling them to pay about $80 for a replacement battery or buy new phones. 
Most of the litigations are filed in federal court in San Jose, California, but lawsuit over the software updates is also awaiting in other federal courts around the country. Lawyers for the consumers, who started filing their complaints by the start of January, have requested a federal judicial panel to consolidate the lawsuit in California. 
Consumers are requesting judges to issue orders that will avoid future adjustments to the iPhone’s operating system which deliberately degrade performance and lowers battery life. They also demanded an amount in compensation and damages. 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) has not responded a request for comment. However, representatives for the Justice Department and SEC declined to comment. About Grant Pasek
